newsitem.title: USA: WMX CEO Phillip Rooney resigns.
newsitem.headline: WMX CEO Phillip Rooney resigns.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc said president and chief executive Phillip Rooney resigned.
Chairman Dean Buntrock will serve as acting chief executive while the WMX board searches for a new CEO from outside the company, it said.
"In addition to the search for a new CEO, the board is also continuing its search for two new independent directors with major corporate experience," WMX said.
Rooney had been CEO of the largest U.S. garbage hauling company only since June 1996. He had previously been WMX chief operating officer from 1984 to 1996.

An investment fund controlled by financier George Soros last week called for Rooney's ouster. The Soros group and other large shareholders of WMX have been pressing the company for months to improve its performance and make major changes.
Shares in WMX were up 1-3/4 to 34-5/8.
WMX said Rooney also gave up his seat on the boards of directors of WMX and its Wheelabrator Technologies Inc and Waste Management International Plc affiliates.

"The board has appointed a search committee and will retain the services of an executive recruiting firm to help identify a new chief executive from outside WMX as quickly as is practicable," the company said.

WMX director Peer Pedersen said, "Phil Rooney was the architect of the plan to focus on our core competencies in waste management and waste-to-energy services, a plan that the board strongly, unanimously and enthusiastically endorses."

Pedersen continued, "We accepted his resignation reluctantly and only because he was determined that our people should not be distracted from the important tasks at hand. While we regret Phil's departure, the board thanks him for putting the company on a firm strategic path."
